The write-up's "finite blocker" fact states: "If a family of finite sets is pairwise intersecting and has a member $C$ of size $r$, then it has only finitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals."

The objection claims this is false with counterexample: E_i = {a_1, ..., a_i, b_i} for i ≥ 1. All sets contain a_1, so pairwise intersecting. Member E_1 = {a_1, b_1} has size 2.

Wait, first let me check the counterexample. The family is F = {E_i : i ≥ 1} where E_i = {a_1, ..., a_i, b_i}. The a's and b's are distinct elements presumably. All E_i contain a_1, so pairwise intersecting. E_1 = {a_1, b_1} has size 2.

Now, what are the transversals (hitting sets) of this family? A transversal X must meet every E_i. Since all E_i contain a_1, {a_1} is a transversal. Also, X could contain b_i for various i, and a_j's.

Is {a_1} a minimal transversal? Yes, it meets every set and is nonempty... well, minimal transversals must be nonempty since the family is nonempty. {a_1} meets every E_i, and any proper subset of {a_1} is empty, which doesn't meet E_1. So {a_1} is an inclusion-minimal transversal.

Is {b_1, a_2} a transversal? It must meet every E_i. E_1 = {a_1, b_1}: contains b_1. ✓. E_2 = {a_1, a_2, b_2}: contains a_2. ✓. E_i for i ≥ 2 contains a_1, ..., a_i ⊇ {a_1, a_2}, so contains a_2. ✓. So {b_1, a_2} meets every E_i.

Is it minimal? Remove b_1: {a_2}. Does {a_2} meet E_1 = {a_1, b_1}? No, a_2 ∉ E_1, b_1 ∉... {a_2} ∩ {a_1, b_1} = ∅. So b_1 is essential. Remove a_2: {b_1}. Does {b_1} meet E_2 = {a_1, a_2, b_2}? b_1 ∉ E_2. So no. Hence a_2 essential. So {b_1, a_2} is an inclusion-minimal transversal.

Is {b_1, b_2, a_3} a transversal? E_1 ∋ b_1 ✓. E_2 ∋ b_2 ✓. E_3 = {a_1,a_2,a_3,b_3} ∋ a_3 ✓. E_i for i ≥ 3 contains a_3. ✓. Minimal: remove b_1: {b_2, a_3} — does it meet E_1? E_1 = {a_1, b_1}, no. Essential. Remove b_2: {b_1, a_3} — meets E_2 = {a_1,a_2,b_2}? No. Essential. Remove a_3: {b_1, b_2} — meets E_3 = {a_1,a_2,a_3,b_3}? No. Essential. Minimal.

In general {b_1, ..., b_{k-1}, a_k} for k ≥ 2: meets E_i via b_i for i < k, and via a_k for i ≥ k. Each element essential (removing b_i fails to meet E_i; removing a_k fails to meet E_k). So infinitely many inclusion-minimal transversals.

So indeed the "finite blocker" claim as stated is FALSE in general: pairwise intersecting + existence of a finite member does NOT imply finitely many minimal transversals.
